results.description:
How a Village Self-Defence Group Turned Into Nigeria’s New Cross-Border Terror Bridge

In 2017, border villages in Sokoto invited an armed herding militia, Lakurawa to shield them from bandits.

By 2026, that former vigilante force had evolved into one of Nigeria’s fastest-spreading terror threats:
• Taxed Kebbi and Sokoto communities ₦50m ($36,000) in March 2026 just to let clerics preach Ramadan tafsir
• Killed 162 civilians in Woro and Nuku, Kwara State after villages rejected its rule
• Built an active corridor linking Sahelian jihadists (ISGS/JNIM) toward northern Benin and central Nigeria

History’s hardest internal security lesson repeats: when the state leaves a vacuum, outsourced community defence rarely stays defensive for long.

results.title: How Can Armed Groups Move So Freely While Communities Remain Under Threat?
results.description:
How Can Armed Groups Move So Freely While Communities Remain Under Threat?

Reports that heavily armed men arrived in convoys at a wedding ceremony in Zamfara State, allegedly linked to a wanted bandit kingpin, have once again raised serious questions about Nigeria’s security system.

Eyewitnesses reportedly said some of the men wore military-style uniforms, while others carried sophisticated weapons. The incident has reignited public concerns over how armed groups continue to operate openly in communities already struggling with insecurity.

Where is the government’s security strategy, and why do residents continue to live in fear? Nigerians deserve answers, not just repeated assurances. When heavily armed groups can reportedly move in convoys without fear, citizens are justified in demanding stronger intelligence, effective security operations, and accountability from those entrusted with protecting lives and property.

For the people of Zamfara, security is not a political slogan. It is the difference between living in peace and going to bed wondering what tomorrow may bring.

How much longer must ordinary Nigerians wait for the safety they deserve?💯😔😈🇳🇬📌

results.title: Lakurawa, Boko Haram and ISWAP do follow jihadist doctrine.
results.description: Lakurawa, Boko Haram and ISWAP do follow jihadist doctrine. In Zamfara the main actors remain profit-driven bandit gangs focused on ransoms, cattle rustling and mining levies from local Muslim communities. Lakurawa is hybrid and expanding from Sokoto/Kebbi with some ties, but the dominant pattern there is still economic banditry.

results.title: The incident is confirmed.
results.description: The incident is confirmed. On Wednesday evening (21 Oct), bandits ambushed a vehicle on the Marnona-Isa road near Kunawa village, Goronyo LGA, Sokoto. Passengers were returning from the state capital; some were recent government recruits for screening. Police verified three killed (driver and two others). Early reports, including from conflict reporter Bakatsine, said everyone aboard died and shared photos; other accounts noted six bodies, injuries, or a missing person. Multiple Nigerian outlets covered it.
